terms.definition: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
terms.function: Gives an element versions with different masses.
terms.whereItIs: The carbon-12 and carbon-14 pair in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Isotopes power dating, medicine, and nuclear energy.

terms.definition: The total number of protons plus neutrons in an atom.
terms.function: Names the isotope — carbon-14 has a mass number of 14.
terms.whereItIs: The 12 in carbon-12 and the 14 in carbon-14.
terms.whyItMatters: The mass number is how each isotope is identified.

terms.definition: The number of protons in an atom, identical across all isotopes of an element.
terms.function: Keeps all isotopes the same element.
terms.whereItIs: The 6 red protons in both nuclei.
terms.whyItMatters: The fixed proton count is what 'same element' means.

terms.definition: The steady breakdown of an unstable isotope, releasing particles and energy.
terms.function: Gives scientists a clock for dating and a tool for medicine and power.
terms.whereItIs: The behavior of carbon-14, hinted by the use icons.
terms.whyItMatters: Decay is what makes isotopes useful and powerful.
